questions.solution_text:
1. **Find where the curves meet by solving $f(x)=g(x)$**
$x^{2}=2x+3$
$x^{2}-2x-3=0$
$(x-3)(x+1)=0$
$x=-1,\ 3$
2. **Decide which curve is upper on each interval by testing a point**
At $x=0$: $3>0$, so the line is upper.
3. **Integrate upper minus lower over each interval**
$\int_{-1}^{3}\left[(2x+3)-x^{2}\right]dx$
$= \left[x^{2}+3x-\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_{-1}^{3}$
$= \left(9+9-9\right)-\left(1-3+\dfrac{1}{3}\right)$
$= 9+\dfrac{5}{3}$
$= \dfrac{32}{3}\ \text{units}^{2}$

questions.solution_text:
1. **Find where the curves meet by solving $f(x)=g(x)$**
$4x=x^{2}$
$x(4-x)=0$
$x=0,\ 4$
2. **Decide which curve is upper on each interval by testing a point**
At $x=1$: $4>1$, so $y=4x$ is upper on $0<x<4$.
At $x=\dfrac{9}{2}$: $\dfrac{81}{4}>18$, so $y=x^{2}$ is upper on $4<x<5$.
3. **Integrate upper minus lower over each interval**
$\int_{0}^{4}\left(4x-x^{2}\right)dx = \left[2x^{2}-\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{4} = 32-\dfrac{64}{3} = \dfrac{32}{3}$
$\int_{4}^{5}\left(x^{2}-4x\right)dx = \left[\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}-2x^{2}\right]_{4}^{5} = -\dfrac{25}{3}-\left(-\dfrac{32}{3}\right) = \dfrac{7}{3}$
4. **Add the areas of the pieces**
$\dfrac{32}{3}+\dfrac{7}{3}$
$= 13\ \text{units}^{2}$

options.why: Found only one of the two pieces and forgot to add the other.
Ignored the second curve and integrated $x^{2}$ all the way from $x=0$ to $x=4$.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Find where the curves meet by solving $f(x)=g(x)$**
$x^{2}=(x-4)^{2}$
$0=-8x+16$
$x=2$
2. **Decide which curve is upper on each interval by testing a point**
The region lies under $y=x^{2}$ from $x=0$ to $x=2$, then under $y=(x-4)^{2}$ to $x=4$.
3. **Integrate upper minus lower over each interval**
$\int_{0}^{2}x^{2}dx = \left[\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{2} = \dfrac{8}{3}$
$\int_{2}^{4}(x-4)^{2}dx = \left[\dfrac{(x-4)^{3}}{3}\right]_{2}^{4} = 0-\left(-\dfrac{8}{3}\right) = \dfrac{8}{3}$
4. **Add the areas of the pieces**
$\dfrac{8}{3}+\dfrac{8}{3}$
$= \dfrac{16}{3}\ \text{units}^{2}$

questions.solution_text:
1. **Find where the curves meet by solving $f(x)=g(x)$**
$x^{2}=k$
$x=-\sqrt{k},\ \sqrt{k}$
2. **Integrate upper minus lower over each interval**
$\int_{-\sqrt{k}}^{\sqrt{k}}\left(k-x^{2}\right)dx$
$= \left[kx-\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_{-\sqrt{k}}^{\sqrt{k}}$
$= 2\left(k^{\frac{3}{2}}-\dfrac{k^{\frac{3}{2}}}{3}\right)$
$= \dfrac{4}{3}k^{\frac{3}{2}}$
Setting this equal to the given area:
$\dfrac{4}{3}k^{\frac{3}{2}}=\dfrac{500}{3}$
$k^{\frac{3}{2}}=125$
$k=125^{\frac{2}{3}}=25$
